result.title: SchemaCaps: When a Compatible Tool Update Silently Widens an AI Agent's Authority
result.comment: Author's accepted version (without the publisher's layout). Accepted at ICAART 2027; final version published by SCITEPRESS. Artefact: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24233014
result.summary: The tools users approve for their AI agents keep changing their JSON input schemas. Of 8 surveyed MCP clients and scanners, none is observed or documented to re-approve a tool whose input schema widens (two not determinable). We define non-amplification over the coordinates visible in the schema (declared arguments and undeclared fields, on effective values) and a re-binding rule decided by subschema inclusion, trusting no field labels by default and conservative up to its checker and tested case analysis. Evidence: a Coq proof of composition; 48 regression tests; an exact-reference benchmark, where the reviewed version of the rule silently re-bound 27 amplifying changes, now fixed; and a pilot on 604 releases of 39 public MCP servers. There, 412 of 580 compatible schema changes widen some coordinate, yet compatibility re-binds them silently. The authors' adjudicated double annotation finds at least 76 that add or widen an authority-bearing argument (66 of the 84 a name-based labeller flags, plus 10 it misses). On existing tools, the rule asks 645 re-approvals, against 1,197 for pinning the input schema (2,004 with descriptions) and 617 for compatibility. Behaviour change behind an identical schema remains out of reach.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究 AI agent 所批准工具的 JSON 输入 schema 变更问题，提出「非放大」判定与基于子 schema 包含关系的重新绑定规则，并用 Coq 证明、回归测试和 MCP 服务器发布数据评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 主题是工具权限与 schema 兼容性审查，未涉及视觉或多模态推理状态、证据使用或停止决策，其子 schema 形式化与 LVR 的联系过于牵强，故排除。
